mergedParams.userDescription: Words gently scaling up from 90% to 100% on appearance. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

prompts.prompt: Create a typography preset that implements a gentle scaling animation for words, starting from 90% scale and growing to 100% as they appear. Think of this like a video editor's 'scale from center' keyframe animation with a smooth ease-out curve. Each word should feel like it's breathing into existence, similar to how you'd animate titles in After Effects with a subtle scale expression. The animation should be staggered across words to create a cascading reveal effect, like ripples moving through the text. Use a BaseLayout container with flex layout to hold TextAtom components for each word. Apply generic keyframe effects with scale transforms that animate from 0.9 to 1.0 over 0.3-0.5 seconds per word. Consider adding a subtle opacity fade from 0.8 to 1.0 to enhance the breathing effect. The timing should be relative to the parent, with each word starting its animation slightly after the previous one (0.05-0.1 second delays). This creates a wave-like progression through the sentence.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2' containing individual TextAtom components for each word. Effects: Use generic keyframe effects with AnimationRange for scale (0.9 to 1.0) and opacity (0.8 to 1.0). Timing: Each word gets a relative startTime offset of index * 0.08 seconds. Animation duration: 0.4 seconds per word with 'ease-out' easing. Performance: Use transform: scale() for GPU acceleration, add will-change: transform, opacity to TextAtom style props. Caption data: If using typography preset type, iterate through captionData.words array and create TextAtom for each word with word.text content. Consider using fitDurationTo: 'children' on the BaseLayout to ensure proper container timing.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic typography preset where words scale up from 90% to 100% with a spring-like bounce effect, mimicking the 'overshoot' animation principle from traditional animation. Imagine setting up animation curves in Premiere Pro where you add ease graphs with a slight overshoot - the scale goes from 0.9 to 1.02, then settles back to 1.0. This creates a more dynamic, playful feel perfect for energetic captions or modern title sequences. Layer this with a subtle blur-to-sharp transition (2px blur to 0) to simulate depth of field changes as the text comes into focus. Each word should feel like it's popping forward from the background. The layout should accommodate both single-line and multi-line text gracefully.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='flex flex-wrap items-baseline justify-start max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4' for responsive multi-line support. Effects: Create internal effect preset 'word-pop' with scale keyframes [0.9, 1.02, 1.0] at ranges [0, 0.7, 1.0] and blur filter from 'blur(2px)' to 'blur(0px)'. Use spring easing or custom cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for bounce. Timing: Stagger words with index * 0.06 seconds delay, total animation time 0.5 seconds per word. Performance: Combine transforms in single property, use filter for blur (GPU accelerated). Typography features: Access captionData.words with relative timing, apply stronger effects to words with metadata.keyword === true or metadata.impact > 0.7 for emphasis.

prompts.prompt: Build a minimalist typokinetic preset that treats the 90% to 100% scale as a subtle breathing rhythm, like adjusting clip speed ramping in a video timeline. Instead of obvious scaling, make it feel like the text is gently inhaling as it appears. Combine this with letter-spacing that contracts from 0.05em to 0em, creating a tightening effect as words settle into place. This is similar to how you'd keyframe tracking in After Effects - starting slightly loose and pulling tight for impact. Add a very subtle rotation correction from -0.5deg to 0deg to give a sense of the text 'locking' into position. Perfect for elegant, professional captions or documentary-style titles.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full' containing TextAtom components with className='inline-block mx-1'. Effects: Generic keyframe effects with multiple properties - scale: [0.9, 1.0], letterSpacing: ['0.05em', '0em'], rotate: [-0.5, 0], opacity: [0, 1]. All animations use 'ease-in-out' over 0.6 seconds. Timing: Words appear sequentially with 0.1 second overlaps (startTime: index * 0.5). Performance: Bundle all transforms into single transform property, avoid layout shifts with fixed dimensions. Caption integration: Use word.relativeTime for precise synchronization with audio/video timeline. Add containerProps.style with minHeight to prevent layout jumps.

prompts.prompt: Create an audio-reactive typokinetic preset where the 90% to 100% scale animation syncs with audio beats or intensity. Think of this like using audio keyframes in After Effects or beat detection in Premiere Pro. Words don't just scale uniformly - they pulse slightly with the audio waveform, scaling between 0.9 and 1.0 based on audio intensity. When there's a beat, words might briefly hit 1.05 scale before settling. This creates a living, breathing text effect that feels connected to the soundtrack. Add a subtle glow effect that intensifies with audio peaks, similar to how you'd link glow intensity to audio amplitude in video editing software.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with nested BaseLayout for each word to handle individual audio reactions. Effects: Use waveform effects with type='scale' reacting to 'bass' frequencies, sensitivity=0.3, threshold=0.5. Base scale animation from 0.9 to 1.0, with waveform adding 0-0.1 additional scale on beats. Glow effect using textShadow with waveform type='custom' modulating shadow blur radius. Audio integration: Fetch audio analysis data using props.fetcher, select impactful beats for enhanced reactions. Timing: Base animation 0.4 seconds, waveform effects continuous. Performance: Use transform-origin: center, GPU-accelerated transforms. Internal effects: Create 'audio-pulse' preset combining scale and glow reactions.

prompts.prompt: Develop a cinematic typokinetic preset that scales words from 90% to 100% while simulating a dolly zoom effect. Imagine setting up a counter-zoom in your video editing timeline - as the text scales up, add a subtle perspective shift that makes it feel like the camera is pulling back. Each word starts slightly below its final position (translateY: 5px) and rises as it scales, creating a floating-up motion. Add a film-grain texture overlay that fades as text becomes fully visible, similar to adding adjustment layers in Premiere. This creates a cinematic, movie-title feel perfect for dramatic captions or opening credits.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative overflow-hidden h-screen flex items-center justify-center' with perspective CSS. TextAtom components with className='transform-gpu'. Effects: Combine scale [0.9, 1.0], translateY [5, 0], and translateZ [20, 0] for dolly zoom effect. Add filter effects for grain: 'contrast(1.1) brightness(0.95)' to 'contrast(1) brightness(1)'. Timing: 0.8 second duration with 'cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)' easing. Create slight random delays (Math.random() * 0.1) for organic feel. Performance: Use transform3d() for hardware acceleration, perspective: 1000px on container. Visual enhancements: Add ::before pseudo-element for grain texture overlay with opacity animation.

prompts.prompt: Design a typewriter-inspired typokinetic preset where words scale from 90% to 100% but with a mechanical, stepped feel. Think of this like creating a stop-motion effect in your video editor - instead of smooth scaling, use stepped easing or frame-by-frame animation. Each word 'types' into existence with 3-4 discrete scale steps (0.9, 0.93, 0.97, 1.0), similar to how you'd create a typewriter effect with hold keyframes. Add a subtle horizontal jitter (translateX: ±1px) on each step to simulate mechanical vibration. Include an optional cursor element that blinks and moves to the next word position, like tracking a null object in After Effects.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='font-mono relative' for typewriter aesthetic. TextAtom with visibility controlled by effects. Cursor as separate ShapeAtom or pseudo-element. Effects: Use steps(4) easing function for scale animation, creating discrete jumps. Add micro translateX animations with Math.random() * 2 - 1 for jitter. Cursor uses infinite opacity animation (blink). Timing: Each word appears over 0.3 seconds with instant steps, 0.15 second pause between words. Performance: Use CSS steps() function for optimal frame stepping, avoid continuous calculations. Typography features: Respect captionData.words timing but quantize to nearest frame (1/30s or 1/60s) for authentic mechanical feel.

prompts.prompt: Create a depth-layered typokinetic preset where words scale from 90% to 100% with simulated z-depth. Like organizing clips on different video tracks with varying scales and opacities, each word exists on a virtual depth layer. Important words (keywords/high impact) start at 85% scale and animate to 100%, while supporting words go from 92% to 100%. Add a depth-of-field blur effect where words outside the 'focus range' have slight blur that sharpens as they scale up. Layer this with subtle color grading - distant words slightly desaturated, becoming vibrant at full scale. This creates a parallax-like text reveal similar to 2.5D animation in After Effects.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Multiple BaseLayout layers with z-index positioning based on word importance. Use containerProps.className='absolute inset-0' for layering. Effects: Conditional scaling based on metadata.impact - high impact words: scale [0.85, 1.0], normal words: [0.92, 1.0]. Blur effect: filter 'blur(1.5px)' to 'blur(0px)' for depth. Color grading via filter: 'saturate(0.7)' to 'saturate(1)'. Timing: High-impact words animate first (startTime: 0), others follow (startTime: 0.2). Performance: Use CSS contain: layout for layer optimization. Caption integration: Use metadata.keyword and metadata.impact to determine depth layers and animation intensity. Consider fitDurationTo: 'scene' for proper scene synchronization.

prompts.prompt: Build a elastic typokinetic preset that treats the 90% to 100% scale as part of a larger elastic motion system. Imagine using the graph editor in After Effects to create custom velocity curves - the scale doesn't just grow linearly but stretches and contracts like elastic material. Words slightly squash (scaleY: 0.85, scaleX: 1.05) before expanding to normal proportions, similar to animation principles of squash and stretch. Add a complementary skew effect that makes text lean forward slightly (-2deg) then straighten as it scales. This creates a playful, cartoon-like motion perfect for dynamic captions or energetic content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3' allowing for elastic deformations. TextAtom with transform-origin: bottom center for proper squash/stretch pivot. Effects: Multi-stage animation - Phase 1: scaleX: 1.05, scaleY: 0.85, skewX: -2deg (0-0.3 range), Phase 2: scaleX: 0.95, scaleY: 1.05, skewX: 1deg (0.3-0.6 range), Phase 3: scale: 1.0, skewX: 0deg (0.6-1.0 range). Use 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.6, 0.32, 1.6)' for elastic easing. Timing: Total duration 0.7 seconds per word, staggered by index * 0.12. Performance: Combine all transforms in single property, use will-change sparingly. Add backface-visibility: hidden to prevent render issues during skew.

prompts.prompt: Design a glitch-inspired typokinetic preset where the 90% to 100% scale happens through digital distortion. Think of adding a glitch effect plugin to your video timeline - words don't smoothly scale but flicker through corrupted states. Create 'data corruption' frames where scale might jump to 1.1, then 0.85, then settle at 1.0, similar to datamoshing techniques in video editing. Add RGB channel splitting during the glitch (red/blue channels offset by ±2px), and occasional position jumps. Include a digital noise texture that appears during scale transitions. Perfect for tech-themed content, gaming videos, or cyberpunk aesthetics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with position: relative, overflow: hidden for glitch containment. Each TextAtom wrapped in BaseLayout for individual glitch effects. Effects: Random scale keyframes [0.9, 1.1, 0.85, 1.05, 1.0] with instant transitions between some frames. RGB split using multiple text-shadow: '2px 0 red, -2px 0 cyan' during glitch moments. Add filter: 'hue-rotate()' with random values during corruption. Timing: Main animation 0.5 seconds with 2-3 glitch moments at random intervals (Math.random()). Performance: Use CSS custom properties for dynamic glitch values, GPU-accelerated filters. Consider using internal effect preset 'glitch-reveal' for reusability. Audio sync: If audio available, trigger stronger glitches on beat impacts.

prompts.prompt: Create a fluid motion typokinetic preset where words scale from 90% to 100% as part of a liquid-like flow. Imagine using flow effects or liquify in After Effects - text doesn't just scale but seems to flow into position like water filling a container. Each word has a subtle wave motion during scaling (using sin/cos wave functions for smooth undulation). Add a water-like refraction effect using CSS filters - slight blur and brightness variations that stabilize as the text reaches full scale. Words should feel like they're surfacing from underwater, with a ripple effect emanating from each word as it appears. Perfect for smooth, organic title animations or wellness/beauty content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full' and clipPath for wave masking. TextAtom with additional wrapper for wave distortion effects. Effects: Scale animation [0.9, 1.0] combined with translateY using sine wave: Math.sin(progress * Math.PI * 2) * 5. Filter effects: 'blur(1px) brightness(1.1)' to 'blur(0px) brightness(1)' simulating water refraction. Optional SVG filter for displacement mapping (water ripple). Timing: 1 second duration with 'ease-in-out', waves continue for 0.3 seconds after scale completes. Performance: Use CSS custom properties for wave calculations, update via animation frames. Ripple effect using radial-gradient with animated size/opacity. Consider using LottieAtom for complex water animations if needed. Caption sync: Use word.relativeTime to create natural flow following speech rhythm.
